stem: A 43-year-old patient has obstruction of intestinal lymphatic drainage. Intestinal epithelial cells still take up glucose and assemble absorbed fatty acids into triglycerides. Which of the following nutrient-transport findings best follows from the obstruction?

options.label: A
options.text: Both nutrients are retained because both leave through lacteals
options.explanation: Glucose normally enters villus capillary blood rather than lymph. A lymphatic obstruction does not block both routes equally.
options.misconception: Incorrectly assigns glucose and triglycerides to the same lymphatic exit.

options.label: B
options.text: Triglyceride export is impaired while glucose reaches portal blood
options.explanation: Reassembled intestinal triglycerides leave through lacteals, while absorbed glucose enters capillary blood and the hepatic portal route. The routes explain the selective effect.
options.misconception: No misconception: lymphatic lipid export and portal glucose transport are distinct.

options.label: C
options.text: Glucose export is impaired while triglycerides reach portal blood
options.explanation: This assigns the nutrients to the wrong exits. Glucose enters blood; intestinal triglyceride transport depends on lymphatic drainage.
options.misconception: Reverses the blood and lymph exit routes of glucose and triglycerides.

options.label: D
options.text: Both nutrients reach portal blood through the same capillary route
options.explanation: The shared portal route applies to absorbed carbohydrates, not to the reassembled intestinal triglycerides described in this case.
options.misconception: Extends the carbohydrate portal route to intestinal triglyceride packages.

options.label: E
options.text: Glucose is redirected into lacteals while triglyceride export rises
options.explanation: Obstruction does not establish a new glucose route through lacteals. It impedes lymphatic lipid export rather than increasing it.
options.misconception: Assumes obstruction creates a new glucose route and increases lipid export.

context:
Learning objective: Distinguish intestinal blood and lymph transport. Entry into an enterocyte and export from it are separate steps; preserved uptake does not prove that lymph-dependent lipid export is intact.

Reassembled intestinal triglycerides leave through lacteals, while absorbed glucose enters capillary blood and the hepatic portal route. The routes explain the selective effect.
